article.Citation/Title: Bowen, W. T., Soskin, R. A., & Chotlos, J. W. (1970). Lysergic acid diethylamide as a variable in the hospital treatment of alcoholism: A follow-up study. Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease, 150(2), 111-118.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Bowen, W. T., Soskin, R. A., & Chotlos, J. W. (1970) Lysergic acid diethylamide.pdf
article.InterventionDescription: Single oral 500-μg LSD dose (25-μg placebo comparator) given during a 60-day inpatient Human Relations Training Laboratory program for hospitalized male alcoholic veterans.

article.Outcome: Primary comparison selected as Table 4 (p.117), which combines Experiments I and II into the article's final, most comprehensive comparison: LSD-500μg-treated patients (n=71, pooled across both experiments) vs all non-500μg comparators (HRTL-only + HRTL+placebo-LSD, n=87). Value taken verbatim from prose immediately following Table 4: 'The percentages of those rated as making a good adjustment, 24 per cent for the LSD group and 27 per cent for the HRTL group.' This prose statement is unambiguous, unlike Table 4's own Poor/Fair cell counts, which show OCR digit-merging artifacts (e.g. '22. 18 | 25; 36 | 54) 17 | 24) 71') that could not be reliably reconstructed and were therefore not used. Table 1 (Experiment I only, N=81, chi2(2)=0.661, first-reported result) and Table 3 (Experiment II only, dose-comparison, chi2=5.738) were considered as alternative primaries -- Table 1 is the first comparison named in the Purpose paragraph and Results, while Table 4 is the paper's summary bottom-line figure the Discussion returns to ('approximately equal in adjustment status after 1 year'). Table 4 was judged the closest to a single stated-primary result because it pools the full study sample rather than a sub-experiment; this is a non-obvious judgment call and a reviewer could reasonably prefer Table 1 instead.
article.SD: Printed directly beneath Table 4 (OCR): 'x2 = 1.468, x2.05 = 5.991.' Degrees of freedom are not explicitly labeled by the authors; df=2 is inferred because the printed critical value 5.991 matches the standard chi-square table's alpha=.05 critical value for df=2, consistent with the 3-category (Poor/Fair/Good) x 2-group table design. This inference is about df labeling only -- the numeric value 1.468 is reported exactly as printed, not altered.
article.PVal: Text states 'The differences in outcome are not statistically significant' in the paragraph introducing Table 4. No exact p-value or explicit threshold symbol (e.g. '<0.05') is printed for this comparison, so per the anti-conversion rule for narrative non-significance language this is coded 'NS' verbatim rather than inferred as a numeric threshold.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 158 = 71 + 87, the Table 4 totals underlying the 24%/27% good-adjustment percentages in Outcome. Cross-checked by addition: 71 = Table 2's LSD-all-patients total (49, completers+followed-up dropouts) + Table 3's LSD-500μg total (22, Experiment II); 87 = Table 2's HRTL-only total (50) + Table 3's placebo-LSD-25μg total (22) + Table 3's no-LSD group (15). Both sums are internally consistent with the printed Table 4 column totals (71 and 87).

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: objective, design, setting, intervention, comparator, outcomes, results, and statistical methods (chi-square with critical values) are all clearly described. Randomization and blinding are described for Experiment II ('through random selection...a double blind experimental procedure'), so both criteria are met for the article even though Experiment I itself was not randomized/blinded. Not met: eligibility (only 'voluntarily applied,' 'male veterans,' and Experiment-II-only contraindication exclusions are given -- no formal inclusion/exclusion list); sample_size_power (no power calculation or sample-size justification anywhere); harms (no adverse-event/safety section, table, or statement exists at all -- not even described as absent); funding_coi (no funding source or conflict-of-interest statement found anywhere in the text). n_met=10 < 13, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 0 (null/negative). Table 4's good-adjustment rate is numerically lower for the LSD group (24%) than the comparator group (27%), and the chi-square is non-significant. The article's own conclusion states 'the long term gains through use of LSD are negligible.'
article.Clincial Trial YN: 1, consistent with the eligibility screen: prospectively planned LSD administration under a defined 60-day inpatient protocol, with assigned regimen (500μg vs 25μg vs none) and prospective 1-year outcome assessment via structured interview.
article.RandomizationYN: Coded 0 for the study underlying the chosen primary Outcome (Table 4). The article's design is genuinely mixed: Experiment II (n=44 of the pooled 158) used explicit random assignment to 500μg vs 25μg dose ('through random selection they would receive either a large or small dose of LSD'), but Experiment I (the larger component of both pooled arms, n=81 of 158) used sequential, non-randomized cohorts -- the LSD group entered Sept 1965-Apr 1966 and the HRTL-only group entered Oct 1966-Apr 1967, after LSD was administratively discontinued from the program, not by random allocation. Because the majority of the pooled Table-4 sample derives from this non-randomized Experiment I comparison, RandomizationYN is coded 0 with this caveat flagged for reviewer override if the field is intended to characterize the article as a whole rather than the specific primary comparison.
article.BlindingYN: Coded 0 for the same reason as RandomizationYN: Experiment II's placebo-dose arm was double-blind, but Experiment I (majority of the pooled Table-4 sample) was open/unblinded, with no placebo control and both groups aware of program assignment. Flagged as a judgment call; a reviewer characterizing the article as a whole rather than the primary comparison might instead prefer 1.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 0 to remain consistent with BlindingYN=0 (must not be 1 when BlindingYN=0). The article does describe a double-blind sub-experiment (Experiment II, 'a double blind experimental procedure was employed'), but this does not characterize the non-blinded Experiment I majority of the pooled primary comparison.
article.Comparator: 1. Two comparator types exist across the pooled Table-4 group: an active no-LSD comparator (HRTL program alone, Experiment I) and a placebo-dose comparator (25μg LSD, Experiment II) -- both are pooled into the single 'HRTL only or HRTL+LSD 25μg' comparator arm (n=87) in Table 4.
article.Power: 0. No a priori or post hoc power calculation, or any discussion of statistical power, appears anywhere in the article.
article.Retention (%): 73.1 = 87 completers / 119 enrolled, calculated for Experiment I only (the only sub-cohort with a disclosed enrolled-vs-completed breakdown). LSD arm: 46 completers (41 analyzed + 5 completed-but-lost-to-follow-up) / 61 enrolled (46 completers + 15 who 'dropped out of their programs prematurely') = 75.4%. HRTL arm: 41 completers (40 analyzed + 1 lost-to-follow-up) / 58 enrolled (41 + 17 dropouts) = 70.7%. Combined: (46+41)/(61+58) = 87/119 = 73.1%. Experiment II is excluded from this calculation because the article states only that '59 alcoholic patients entered and completed the alcoholic program' -- completers are given but the original enrolled/entering count before completion is not disclosed for Experiment II, so a single study-wide retention percentage spanning both experiments is not calculable; the reported 73.1% reflects Experiment I only.
article.ConfoundYN: 1. The article explicitly analyzes several confounding/moderating factors against outcome: pretreatment employment level (Table 5, Hollingshead classification), marital status (Table 6), education, age (dichotomized at the sample median of 44.5 years), timing of LSD administration within the program (Table 8), and program completion status (Table 7).
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: 0. Only minimal, implicit criteria are given -- 'male veterans who had voluntarily applied for the alcoholic treatment program' -- and, for Experiment II only, that 6 of 65 candidates were 'denied the drug on the basis of physical or psychiatric contraindications.' No formal inclusion/exclusion criteria list (diagnostic criteria, age limits, comorbidity exclusions) is stated for study entry generally.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: 0. The primary outcome measure is an 'empirically derived 8-point scale' devised by the authors themselves, validated only informally ('excellent agreement was obtained between scale ratings and the social worker's subjective impressions'), not an externally validated psychometric instrument. The Chwelos Scale (cited to Chwelos et al. 1959) is used to rate depth of LSD response as a secondary correlate, not as the study's SUD outcome measure, so it does not satisfy this field either.
article.Funding/COI YN: 0. No funding source, grant support, or conflict-of-interest disclosure appears anywhere in the article text as OCR'd.
article.BaseStatus: Coded '.' -- the article never characterizes baseline alcoholism severity (e.g., years of drinking, DSM-equivalent severity, prior treatment failures) with language mapping to Mild/Moderate/Severe. Patients are described only as veterans admitted to an inpatient VA alcoholism treatment program.
article.Age_Median: Bracket '30-50' derived from two convergent figures: Experiment I mean ages of 43.8 (LSD group) and 46.1 (HRTL group), and the combined-sample median age of 44.5 years used for dichotomization in the age-outcome analysis ('either above or below 44.5 years'). Both fall within the 30-50 bracket.
article.PercentFem: 0. 'All subjects were male veterans' (Experiment I Subjects paragraph); no female participants are described anywhere in either experiment.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Coded '.' -- race/ethnicity of the sample is never reported anywhere in the article.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: 1. The article reports occupational level using the Hollingshead classification, explicitly including lower-SES categories ('Skilled, semiskilled, unskilled -- Hollingshead positions 5-7', n=89) alongside higher-SES categories (Table 5), which describes inclusion of low-occupational-status participants, though the field's example criteria (income, low-income eligibility, public-insurance enrollment) are not stated verbatim. Judgment call.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: US. Study conducted at the Topeka Veterans Administration Hospital, Topeka, Kansas (footnote 1: '2200 Gage Boulevard, Topeka, Kansas 66622').
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: 1. Patients were routine VA hospital admissions who 'voluntarily applied for the alcoholic treatment program,' reflecting a real-world clinical population of hospitalized alcoholic veterans rather than a healthy-volunteer or highly research-screened sample. Caveat: Experiment II adds a further layer of self-selection within that population -- only 44 of 59 program completers 'volunteered' to be randomized to LSD dose, with 9 refusing and 6 excluded for contraindications -- which somewhat narrows representativeness for that sub-experiment.
article.InterventionDescription: Summarized from the LSD program Methods section (500μg oral dose, single session, 60-day inpatient program, HRTL component) and the Experiment II placebo dose (25μg).
article.HarmsAssessed: 0, consistent with SafetyReported='N'. No section, table, or statement addressing adverse events, side effects, or safety of the LSD sessions appears anywhere in the article. The 8-point outcome scale's 'No DTs or convulsions' item is a post-treatment adjustment criterion scored at 1-year follow-up, not an in-study harms/AE assessment of the LSD dosing sessions themselves.
article.Followup in months: 12. 'All patients in the study were followed up by a research social worker 1 year after discharge from the program.' The Discussion mentions a separate, currently-ongoing 'revised LSD program' with 4-month and 1-year return visits, but this describes a different, later program under development, not additional follow-up of this study's cohort, so it is not used to extend the Followup value.
article.BehaviorChangeMeasured: 1. Abstinence (a use-frequency/behavioral outcome) is directly scored within the 8-point adjustment scale ('Abstinent 6 months or more,' 'Abstinent 11 or 12 months').
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: 1, judgment call. 'No DTs or convulsions' is one of the 8 scale points and reflects a physical/medical withdrawal-related complication rather than a laboratory biomarker or vital sign; coded 1 as the closest fit to 'physical or biological outcomes measured.'
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: 0. The interview covered 'personal adjustment' broadly, but no depression/anxiety/well-being scale or distinct mental-health outcome is scored or reported as part of this study's own measured outcomes (the Discussion cites other studies' mental-health findings, not this study's).
article.RelapseMeasured: 0, judgment call. Abstinence status at the single 1-year follow-up point is scored, but no explicit tracking of relapse/return-to-use as a distinct longitudinal construct (e.g., time-to-relapse, relapse after a period of confirmed sobriety) is described.
article.SafetyReported: N. No Adverse Events, Safety, or Side-Effects section, table, or explicit statement exists anywhere in the article; the text is entirely silent on harms of the LSD sessions.
article.AE_denominator: '.' (never 'NA' per convention) because no safety assessment was reported.
article.ArmScope: NA because SafetyReported='N'; no AE values exist to scope to an arm.
article.EligibleYN: Y. (a) Clinical trial: prospectively planned LSD dosing under a defined hospital protocol with assigned regimen and prospective 1-year outcome assessment -- passes. (b) SUD outcome: abstinence is directly scored within the primary 8-point adjustment scale ('Abstinent 6 months or more') -- passes.

config_proposal.note: Table 4 (combined Experiments I & II) reports good-adjustment rates of 17/71 (24%) for LSD-500μg vs 23/87 (27%) for the pooled non-500μg comparator. The printed inferential statistic (chi2(2)=1.468, Table 4) is a 3-category (Poor/Fair/Good) statistic with df=2, inferred from the printed critical value 5.991 matching the standard df=2 table -- this does not meet the 1-df chi-square requirement in CONVERSION_RULES for a clean/approx chi2 conversion. Instead, collapsing the 3-category outcome to binary good/not-good yields OR = (17/54)/(23/64) = 0.876 (rounded 0.88), offered as an approx-confidence proportion-to-OR conversion per the framework's stated allowance for this transformation. A methodologist should confirm the good/not-good collapse is an appropriate representation of the outcome before ratifying; Table 1 (Experiment I only, chi2(2)=0.661, N=81) is a defensible alternative primary if reviewers prefer the first-reported sub-experiment over the pooled analysis.
